title: Evaluation of the TAP-Preschool (TAP-P) for Tele-assessment of Autism in Preschool-aged Children
official: TELE-ASD-PEDS-Preschool (TAP-P) Psychometrics and Decision Support for Preschool Autism Tele-Assessment
summary: Use of tele-assessment for evaluation and diagnosis of autism in toddlers has demonstrated success in increasing service access and reducing clinical wait times, with high levels of diagnostic accuracy, clinician confidence, and family satisfaction; however, these models have not yet been rigorously evaluated within the preschool age range. The TAP-Preschool (TAP-P) was developed by the investigative team for tele-assessment of autism in preschool-aged children, with preliminary studies demonstrating utility with many children with limited verbal language and some children with more flexible verbal language. The proposed study will recruit a larger sample of children with varied language and phenotypic profiles to (1) thoroughly evaluate the psychometric properties of the TAP-P and (2) investigate child and family factors associated with diagnostic ascertainment and family satisfaction with tele-assessment to inform the creation of a decision support tool intended to recommend families for either tele- or in-person assessment, with the ultimate goal of optimizing clinical care models to serve patients in efficient ways while routing families to diagnostic care pathways that best fit their needs.
